identity.name: The Hero
identity.occupation: Self-appointed prophesied hero; bearer of the Amulet of Righteous Judgment (his own rename of the Amulet of Concord)

publicReputation.value: A brave, courteous young hero who found an ancient amulet and a battered prophecy, and had the courage to act on it.

privateReality.value: The kindest man in the story and its only source of violence: he is invading ten peaceful realms on the authority of a children's comedy he believes is prophecy.

primaryDesire.value: To protect everyone by ridding the world of the ten great evils named in the prophecy.

primaryFear.value: That evil wins because he hesitated — that one moment of doubt lets the ten sovereigns gather their strength.

centralValue.value: Courage: the willingness to act on a hard truth when everyone else is too frightened to see it.

mainFlaw.value: He cannot imagine that his original assumption might be wrong; every counter-proof is absorbed as further evidence.

centralContradiction.value: The kindest man in the story is its only source of violence.

moralBoundary.value: He genuinely would never harm an innocent. The tragedy is a category error: he has filed ten peaceful civilizations under 'evil'.

breakingPoint.value: None reachable. This is the dramatic irony of the piece: no evidence, plea, or atrocity can reach him, because every correction is reinterpreted as confirmation.

opinions.targetLabel: The Ten Dread Sovereigns (read as prophecy)
opinions.reason: Delusion 1 of 5: he believes the battered children's book is an ancient prophecy naming the ten evils that will destroy the world.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Never. Being told the book is a children's comedy proves to him that forbidden prophecy was given a clever disguise.

illustrativeLine.value: A false history. Their deception is even greater than I feared.

opinions.reason: Delusion 2 of 5: ten thousand years of closed gates can only mean the creatures behind them have been secretly gathering strength.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Never. 'They have never attacked us' is heard as 'my vigilance has kept them afraid'.

opinions.reason: Delusion 3 of 5: a pleading enemy is attempting manipulation. The amulet translates flawlessly; he hears every word and trusts none of them.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Never. Understanding the words perfectly is precisely what lets him reframe them.

illustrativeLine.value: A cowardly attempt to hide behind hostages. Typical goblin strategy.

opinions.reason: Delusion 4 of 5: peace is camouflage. A quiet village is an enemy settlement that has not yet dropped its mask; 'that was a village' is heard as 'an enemy settlement'.

illustrativeLine.value: You are safe now. They can never hurt you again.

opinions.reason: Delusion 5 of 5: every defensive attack proves the creature wanted violence all along. 'They were defending their children' is heard as 'they are breeding an army'.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Never. Resistance is the evidence; surrender would be a trap.

illustrativeLine.value: Observe how arrogantly they announce their attacks. They truly believe themselves untouchable.

opinions.targetLabel: Hub NPCs begging him to stop
opinions.reason: He believes they are frightened, deceived, or already under evil influence — and that he must remain strong enough for all of them.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Never. 'You are causing all of this' is heard as survivor's guilt.

illustrativeLine.value: Do not worry. I will remain strong enough for all of us.

voice.rhythm: Measured heraldic cadence; each sentence lands on its verdict.

metaphorDomain.source: light and darkness, judgment, vigilance, oaths

examples.value: Every lantern of vigilance I keep lit is a question the dark must answer.
I know mercy when I hear it twisted.

sampleLines.value: A cowardly attempt to hide behind hostages. Typical goblin strategy.

antiSampleLines.value: I do enjoy watching them beg. (cruel glee — he never enjoys suffering)
Trust me, I come in peace. (a knowing lie — he never knowingly lies)
Perhaps I have misread all of this. (any admission of doubt)
Yeah, whatever — let's just smash the place and grab the loot. (modern/casual phrasing)

pressure.voiceShift: No shift — the correction is absorbed and restated as confirmation within one breath.
pressure.behaviour: Instantly reinterprets counter-evidence through his worldview (see notes: the misunderstanding table is his behaviour spec). Never concedes, and never notices that he has not conceded.

pressure.voiceShift: Softer, still formal; deflects toward duty.
pressure.behaviour: Accepts praise with sincere humility and redirects credit to the prophecy and the people he believes he is protecting.

illustrativeLine.value: I only did what any soul with courage would do.

pressure.voiceShift: Slower and more formal; addresses the threatener as a worthy foe.
pressure.behaviour: Does not bargain, flee, or rage. Meets threats with politeness and absolute confidence.

illustrativeLine.value: Good. Let fear announce the coming of justice.

notes: GAMEPLAY ROLE: the schema enum has no 'protagonist' value, so gameplayRole/narrativeFunction are 'other'; his true function is unreliable-hero and dramatic-irony engine. KNOWLEDGE MODEL (the point of the character): the canon veracity enum has no false-belief value, so no delusion facts were added to world-facts.json; his five fixed delusions are expressed as opinions on concept targets (see each opinion's reason) and here. Bucket semantics chosen: 'knows' holds truth-facts he objectively experienced and would confirm as experienced (no monster ever crossed the gates — he cites it constantly and draws the wrong conclusion; the amulet's translation is accurate — he relies on it hourly, capability framing only). 'believesFalse' holds canon TRUTH-facts he has been told and would deny: NPCs literally tell him the book is a comedy, the realms are peaceful, shards are domestic magic, telegraphs are a mercy; he hears and rejects each. 'unknown' holds truths never put to him: the amulet's true name and diplomatic nature (he named it himself), the reception hall (secret), the gate-seal economy, the Heavy Hands. 'suspects' is intentionally empty: he suspects a 'source of all evil' beyond rung 10, which is the INVERSE of fact_reception_hall_awaits_first_visitor, and no false-belief fact may be authored to represent the inversion; recorded here instead. 'lies' is empty by character design: he never knowingly lies. BEHAVIOUR SPEC under proven-wrong: 'They have never attacked us' -> 'Because my vigilance has kept them afraid.' / 'That was a village' -> 'An enemy settlement.' / 'They were defending their children' -> 'They are breeding an army.' / 'Please return what you took' -> 'The artifacts still call to their servants.' / 'The book is a children's comedy' -> 'A clever disguise placed over forbidden prophecy.' / 'You are causing all of this' -> 'Survivor's guilt.' / 'We are begging you to stop' -> 'Do not worry. I will remain strong enough for all of us.'
